newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: CRICKET-S.AFRICA WANT LESS CRICKET ON ENGLAND TOUR.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-S.AFRICA WANT LESS CRICKET ON ENGLAND TOUR.

text.p: South African cricket chief Ali Bacher wants his country to have a more streamlined tour of England next year.

Bacher, managing director of the United Cricket Board of South Africa (UCBSA), outlined his aim on Thursday following his return from the International Cricket Council (ICC) annual meeting in London earlier in the week.
"I met with Tim Lamb, my counterpart in England, and requested that South Africa plays only one four-day game between tests next year," Bacher told a news conference.

"I spoke to the Austalian manager Geoff Marsh and he said that his team were having trouble peaking in England after a tough tour to South Africa and that they were not helped by having to play two three-day games between each test.

"Bob Woolmer, the coach of the South African team, told me that he felt South Africa would have had enough cricket prior to the test series to make one four-day game a preferable option, giving the team Monday, Tuesday and Wednesday to prepare for the test."
Bacher also said South Africa would be sending an A team to Ireland and Scotland in 1999.
"This is in line with the ICC's wish to spread the game and bring on the countries which they feel can become genuine international teams in the future."
